lines: Progressive shortness of breath, nonproductive cough, and low-grade fevers for 3 weeks.

He has not been on antiretroviral therapy and does not know his most recent CD4 count.

lines: Progressive dyspnea, nonproductive cough, fever, night sweats, and 10-pound weight loss over one month.

lines: Multiple bright red nodules on skin for 3 weeks that bleed easily when traumatized.

He reports the onset of multiple bright red nodules on his skin that are painless but bleed easily when traumatized.
He has not been adherent to his antiretroviral therapy for the past 6 months.

encounters.cc: Profuse watery diarrhea 5-6 times daily with abdominal cramping for 10 days after returning from Peru.

lines: Profuse watery diarrhea 5-6 times daily with abdominal cramping for 10 days after returning from Peru.

This 33-year-old male with AIDS, history of Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia and bacillary angiomatosis, and six months of antiretroviral non-adherence, reports recently returning from a 2-week hiking trip in Peru.
The diarrhea is profuse, occurring 5-6 times per day, and is not bloody.
- Opioid use disorder (in recovery with history of intravenous use)
His past medical history is significant for HIV infection, for which he has not been taking antiretroviral therapy.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg/actuation, 2 inhalations every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing/shortness of breath
- Bictegravir/Tenofovir alafenamide/Emtricitabine (Biktarvy) 50/25/200 mg tablet daily - prescribed but patient non-adherent for past 6 months
On physical examination, he appears dehydrated.
Abdominal examination reveals mild diffuse tenderness without rebound or guarding.
Stool studies are negative for bacterial pathogens, ova, and parasites on microscopy.
A stool antigen test for Cryptosporidium is positive.

encounters.cc: Follow-up evaluation two days after returning from hiking trip in the Rocky Mountains where he experienced altitude-related symptoms.

lines: Follow-up evaluation two days after returning from hiking trip in the Rocky Mountains where he experienced altitude-related symptoms.

The patient is a 34-year-old male with HIV/AIDS (non-adherent to antiretroviral therapy), asthma, and a history of opportunistic infections including Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, bacillary angiomatosis, and cryptosporidiosis, returning for follow-up two days after a hiking trip in the Rocky Mountains where he spent a week at elevations above 10,000 feet.

He reports that he experienced mild headaches, dizziness, and shortness of breath during his first day at altitude but was advised to begin a medication by a local physician to help him acclimate more quickly.
After taking the medication, he noticed he began urinating more frequently and his headaches improved.
On return home, he feels completely back to baseline.
The medication he took is known to decrease renal bicarbonate reabsorption by acting in the proximal tubule.
- Opioid use disorder (in recovery with history of intravenous use)
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg/actuation, 2 inhalations every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing/shortness of breath
- Bictegravir/Tenofovir alafenamide/Emtricitabine (Biktarvy) 50/25/200 mg tablet daily - prescribed but patient non-adherent for past 6 months
He denies any chest pain, palpitations, or cough.

encounters.cc: Persistent shortness of breath, lightheadedness, difficulty sleeping, and occasional headache after returning from Andes mountains.

lines: Persistent shortness of breath, lightheadedness, difficulty sleeping, and occasional headache after returning from Andes mountains.
This 35-year-old with HIV/AIDS and prior altitude illness presents following Andes travel.
During the climb he developed persistent shortness of breath, lightheadedness, difficulty sleeping, and occasional headache, but denied chest pain, cough, or fever.
- Opioid use disorder (in recovery with history of intravenous use)
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg/actuation, 2 inhalations every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing/shortness of breath
- Bictegravir/Tenofovir alafenamide/Emtricitabine (Biktarvy) 50/25/200 mg tablet daily - prescribed but patient non-adherent for past 6 months
On examination in the clinic, his pulse is 96/min, respirations are 20/min, blood pressure is 118/74 mmHg, and oxygen saturation on room air is 90%.
He appears comfortable at rest and lung auscultation is clear without wheezes or rales.
Neurologic and cardiovascular examinations are normal.
Laboratory studies reveal an arterial blood gas with elevated pH and decreased PaCO₂.

encounters.cc: Found unresponsive at home by friends after suspected relapse of heroin use.

lines: Found unresponsive at home by friends after suspected relapse of heroin use.
The patient is a 35-year-old male with HIV infection, history of opportunistic infections, and non-adherence with antiretroviral therapy, who has opioid use disorder in recovery.
He is brought to the emergency department by his friends after they found him unresponsive at home.
His friends report that he has a history of heroin use but had been in a rehabilitation program and was believed to be clean for the past three months.
The patient's friends deny any knowledge of what substances he might have taken.
- Opioid use disorder (in recovery with history of intravenous use)
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg/actuation, 2 inhalations every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing/shortness of breath
- Bictegravir/Tenofovir alafenamide/Emtricitabine (Biktarvy) 50/25/200 mg tablet daily - prescribed but patient non-adherent for past 6 months
Vital signs are as follows: BP 110/70 mmHg, HR 55 bpm, Temperature 36.6°C (97.9°F), and SpO2 88% on room air.
On examination, the patient is somnolent but arousable to painful stimuli.
His respiratory rate is 6 breaths per minute, and breath sounds are shallow.
Pupils are 4 mm and reactive to light.
His skin is warm and dry.
Blood glucose is 98 mg/dL. A urine drug screen is pending.

encounters.cc: High-grade fever, cough, and difficulty breathing after returning from country with ongoing outbreak of highly contagious respiratory virus.

lines: High-grade fever, cough, and difficulty breathing after returning from country with ongoing outbreak of highly contagious respiratory virus.

The patient with HIV/AIDS (non-adherent), asthma, and prior Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia recently returned from a country with an ongoing outbreak of a highly contagious respiratory virus known to cause severe respiratory distress syndrome.
- Opioid use disorder (in recovery with history of intravenous use)
His medical history is significant for asthma.
He takes uses an albuterol inhaler as needed.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg/actuation, 2 inhalations every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing/shortness of breath
- Bictegravir/Tenofovir alafenamide/Emtricitabine (Biktarvy) 50/25/200 mg tablet daily - prescribed but patient non-adherent for past 6 months
Respiratory rate of 28 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation is 89% on room air
Tachypneic and diffuse bilateral crackles are heard on auscultation
Chest X-ray shows bilateral interstitial infiltrates
Public health officials have identified the virus as highly transmissible with significant morbidity and mortality rates, and have recommended isolation and antiviral treatment for all cases.
The patient refuses any treatment, stating he believes in natural healing and fears potential side effects of medications.
